annualCost.label: Yearly federal costs, from the published accounts
annualCost.note: Re-sample after each fiscal year closes. Each item carries its own source.

price.label: Unit costs the government publishes for its own purchases
price.note: Each item carries its own source. A weapon price moves with the contract, not the calendar.

total.label: Lump sums, counted once and still running
total.note: These are cumulative totals, not yearly rates. They only grow.

groups.title: The scale of it
groups.lede: Your whole working life, laid against one year of federal spending. The unit is the second.

groups.title: Pissed away
groups.lede: No war in this group. This is money that bought nothing at all.

groups.title: Bought in your name
groups.lede: Not frivolous. Deliberate. Your share of what the money was used to do.

groups.title: The good it does
groups.lede: The programmes people defend when they defend the tax. Priced honestly, including where they hold up.

items.label: of all federal spending
items.note: Outlays were $7.0 trillion in the 2025 fiscal year. That is what your life's work bought at the till.

source.label: CBO, Monthly Budget Review, fiscal year 2025

items.label: of interest on the national debt
items.note: Net interest passed $1 trillion a year for the first time in 2025. It buys nothing. It is rent on money already spent.

source.label: CBO, Monthly Budget Review, fiscal year 2025

items.label: of the deficit on its own
items.note: The 2025 shortfall was $1.8 trillion. Nobody has paid for that part yet. Somebody will.

source.label: CBO, Monthly Budget Review, fiscal year 2025

items.label: of payments the government admits were wrong
items.note: Fifteen agencies reported $186 billion of improper payments in 2025, across 64 programmes. The running total since 2003 is about $3 trillion.

items.label: of the salaries of all 535 members of Congress
items.note: 535 voting members at $174,000 each. They set that figure themselves and have not moved it since January 2009.

source.label: CRS 97-1011, Salaries of Members of Congress

items.label: of the unemployment money that was simply stolen
items.note: GAO puts pandemic unemployment fraud between $100 billion and $135 billion. This card uses the low end. States have clawed back about $1.2 billion of it.

items.label: of California's high-speed railway
items.note: Voters were told $33 billion in 2008. The 2026 business plan says $126.3 billion. No passenger has ridden it.

source.label: California High-Speed Rail Authority, 2026 draft business plan

items.label: federal agencies used a quarter or less of their headquarters
items.note: GAO measured real attendance against building capacity over three weeks in 2023. You pay the lease, the heat and the light on the empty desks.
The Marine Corps bought 38 Block V missiles for $85.1 million. That is {price} each, used once.

items.singular: hour of an F-35 in the air
items.plural: hours of an F-35 in the air
items.note: {price} an hour, everything counted: fuel, parts, contractors, overhead. One hour.

items.singular: year of holding one person in federal prison
items.plural: years of holding one person in federal prison
items.note: {price} a year. The Bureau of Prisons publishes this figure itself, in the Federal Register.

source.label: Annual Determination of Average Cost of Incarceration Fee, FY2024

items.label: of the property police have taken since 2000
items.note: At least $68.8 billion forfeited by state and federal agencies. Under civil forfeiture the owner need never be charged with a crime.

source.label: Institute for Justice, Policing for Profit

items.label: of the wars fought since 2001
items.note: About $8 trillion. At least 940,000 people died in the direct violence: civilians, soldiers on every side, contractors, journalists and aid workers.

items.label: if your Social Security tax had stayed yours
items.note: The average retired worker collects {price} a year, and half collect less. Your own benefit depends on an earnings history this page never asks for.

source.label: SSA, average monthly benefit for a retired worker

items.singular: year of Medicare for one person
items.plural: years of Medicare for one person
items.note: Medicare cost $1.21 trillion in 2025, spread across 70 million people. That is {price} each.

items.singular: year of public school for one child
items.plural: years of public school for one child
items.note: {price} a year, for one pupil. That is current spending only. Buildings and debt are counted separately.
